notes.entry: - `Ellwood2020comparison` — Design: systematic review of 32 systematic reviews and national guidelines (2009–2019) comparing manual therapy, probiotics, proton pump inhibitors and simethicone for colic. Result: reported probiotics most effective for breastfed infants (crying reduced 25–65 min/day, high-level evidence), manual therapy moderate/low evidence (−33 to −76 min/day), simethicone no benefit, PPIs not supported; guidelines unanimously recommend education and reassurance. Limitation: heterogeneous subpopulations and outcomes make superiority hard to distinguish; umbrella design inherits the biases of the included reviews. Synthesis use: cross-treatment comparison and the guideline-vs-evidence gap.

section_headings: Comparison of common interventions for the treatment of infantile colic: a systematic review of reviews and guidelines.

notes.entry: - `GutirrezCastrelln2017efficacy` — Design: systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis of 32 RCTs, 2242 infants, 9 intervention nodes, published 1960–2015. Result: showed L. reuteri DSM 17938 ranked best (WMD −51.3, 95% CI −72.2 to −30.5, reported in hours; SUCRA best treatment), dietary approaches second (WMD −37.4, CI −56.1 to −18.7); simethicone/dicyclomine/herbal lacked evidence. Limitation: heterogeneity and inconsistency among trials could overestimate effects; predates the null Australian trial's full weight; units in the report are ambiguous (labelled hours), so use the ranking qualitatively rather than the point estimate. Synthesis use: comparative ranking of interventions, qualitative only.

section_headings: Efficacy of Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 for infantile colic: Systematic review with network meta-analysis.
Study protocol register and search strategy

notes.entry: - `Sung2014treating` — Design: double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial, 167 breastfed and formula-fed infants under 3 months with colic (modified Wessel criteria), community sample in Melbourne; L. reuteri DSM 17938 1×10⁸ CFU/day vs placebo for 1 month. Result: found no benefit — the probiotic group cried or fussed 49 min/day MORE at 1 month (95% CI 8 to 90, P=0.02), mainly more fussing in formula-fed infants; no differences in sleep, maternal mental health, microbial diversity, or calprotectin. Limitation: mostly emergency-department recruitment, faecal analyses on a subset, L. reuteri colonisation detected in only 45% of treated infants. Synthesis use: the key contrary trial — the largest and most rigorous single RCT, null in the only trial including formula-fed infants; used as the narrative turn.
